import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 351

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/351](https://www.erdosproblems.com/351)
-/

open Polynomial

namespace Erdos351

/-- The set of rational numbers of the form `P(n) + 1 / n` where `n` is a natural number
and `P` is a polynomial with rational coefficients.

Note: We include `P 0` in there (since `1 / 0 = 0`), but this doesn't change the validity of the
conjecture -/
def imageSet {α : Type*} [Semifield α] (P : α[X]) : Set α :=
  Set.range (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ P.eval ↑n + 1 / n)

/-- The predicate that a set `A` is strongly complete, i.e. that for every finite set `B`, every sufficiently
large integer is a sum of elements of the set `A \ B`. -/
def IsStronglyComplete {α : Type*} [Semiring α] (A : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∀ B : Finset α,
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ↑m ∈ { ∑ n ∈ X, n | (X : Finset α) (_ : ↑X ⊆ A \ B) }

/-- The predicate that the rational polynomial `P` has a complete image. -/
def HasCompleteImage (P : ℚ[X]) : Prop := IsStronglyComplete (imageSet P)

/--
Let $p(x) \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ be a non-constant rational polynomial with positive leading
coefficient. Is it true that $$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$ is strongly complete,
in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers? -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos351.lean"]
theorem erdos_351 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ P : ℚ[X], 0 < P.natDegree → 0 < P.leadingCoeff → HasCompleteImage P := by
  sorry

/--
Let $p(x) = x \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. It has been shown that
$$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$
is strongly complete, in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
protected theorem erdos_351.variants.X : HasCompleteImage X := by
  sorry

/-- Let $p(x) = x ^ 2 \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. It has been shown that
$$A=\{ p(n)+1/n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$$
is strongly complete, in the sense that, for any finite set $B$,
$$\left\{\sum_{a \in X} a : X \subseteq A \setminus B, X \textrm{ is finite}\right\}$$
contains all sufficiently large integers. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_351.variants.X_sq : HasCompleteImage (X ^ 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos351

reformulations.difference: The natural-number index includes n = 0, whereas the source uses positive integers. In the rational specialization, this adds P.eval 0 because 1 / 0 = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing A₊ for the positive-index image, imageSet P = insert (P.eval 0) A₊. Strong completeness is invariant under adjoining one element: in the reverse direction, include that element in the finite deletion set; the forward direction follows by monotonicity. Proved imageSet_eq_insert_positive and hasCompleteImage_iff_positive in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the file's sorry-backed theorems.

reformulations.difference: The definition quantifies over Finset deletion sets and eventually over natural-number targets; the source describes finite subsets B ⊆ A and sufficiently large integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For A ⊆ ℚ, finite sets and Finsets represent the same deletion choices. Arbitrary finite B can be replaced by B ∩ A without changing A \ B. Sufficiently large natural and integer targets are equivalent after choosing a nonnegative threshold. The set-builder expands to an existential finite subset with the required sum, not a vacuous implication. Proved the full equivalence in stronglyComplete_iff_source_subsets in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The original book formulates the problem for the sequence (P(n) + 1/n), with completeness of every tail; Lean uses its set of values and finite deletions of values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every permitted nonconstant positive-leading polynomial, P(n+1) − P(n) − 1/(n(n+1)) is positive eventually. Thus the sequence is eventually injective, and each value has finitely many preimages. Any finite set of forbidden values can therefore be avoided by an injective tail. Conversely, deleting the finitely many values of an initial segment ensures that chosen values have representatives beyond that segment. Consequently the sequence and set formulations of strong completeness agree.

reformulations.difference: The full corrected formulation in the solution paper's Corollary 7 also allows P = 0 and positive constant polynomials; Lean states the nonconstant positive-leading case.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted cases follow from the elementary Egyptian-fraction lemma (Lemma 3). For c = u/v > 0 and a large integer m, take k = ceil(vm/u) − 1 and r = vm − uk, so 1 ≤ r ≤ u. For each of these finitely many r, Lemma 3 supplies exactly k distinct denominators beyond any prescribed cutoff with reciprocal sum r/v once k is large. Their c + 1/n values sum to kc + r/v = m. The c = 0 case follows directly from the same lemma without prescribing the number of terms. Thus adjoining the constant cases is an elementary equivalent extension of the corrected problem, not a missing substantive hypothesis.

The May 2026 paper proves the affirmative corrected problem, and its Corollary 7 specializes to both X and X²; this supports the recorded solved categories and answer(True). The paper explicitly documents the necessary positivity correction to the original book's unqualified question.
